title: Microsoft CEO Nadella: I Have Become an AGI Believer, But AI Has Absolutely No Consciousness
excerpt: At a time when AI technology is advancing at breakneck speed, the judgments of tech giants' executives about the future always attract close attention. Accordin
content_html:
At a time when AI technology is advancing at breakneck speed, the judgments of tech giants' executives about the future always attract close attention. According to the tech media outlet The Verge, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella admitted during a roundtable discussion that he has now become an "AGI believer."

On AGI belief: a perspective grounded in political and economic organizational structures

As for why he believes in the arrival of AGI (artificial general intelligence), Nadella offered a very pragmatic perspective. He pointed out that the reason he firmly believes AGI will eventually be achieved is that we need to think deeply at the economic level: as AGI evolves, what kind of organizational structure will the future political and economic system form?

Drawing a clear bottom line: denying that AI has consciousness and agreeing not to grant it moral status

Although he is convinced of AGI's macroeconomic impact, Nadella is very firm on the question of whether AI has subjective consciousness. He explicitly stated that frontier AI models like Claude do not have consciousness.

At the same time, Nadella agreed with a previous view by Microsoft AI head Suleyman, namely that companies should not grant rights to AI models, nor should they regard them as beings that may have moral status. Previously, Suleyman had publicly warned that the Anthropic team had fallen into a state of "self-hypnosis," and that this approach is highly dangerous.

Focusing on real-world pain points: the most important task now is solving the social problems of AI adoption

Rather than discussing ethereal consciousness or hypnotic states, Nadella believes the industry's current focus should return to reality. He stressed that the most important and urgent issue for the AI industry to solve remains a social one, namely that it must ensure the existing economic system can enable the widest possible adoption of AI technology.
